clusters.headline: Veteran Ugandan opposition leader collapses in court and in ICU, his wife says
clusters.summary: The 70 year old has been in detention since November 2024 and faces treason charges, which he denies.

clusters.headline: China's top leaders set to hold October meeting on internal governance, pledge measures to support economy
clusters.summary: The top decision-making body of the ruling Communist party, the Politburo, acknowledged "difficulties and challenges facing the economy" at its meeting.

clusters.headline: Singapore must strengthen talent pipeline of business events industry to stay competitive: Gan Siow Huang
clusters.summary: At the same event, former Speaker of Parliament Tan Chuan-Jin gave practical advice on how leaders in the business events industry can inspire the people they lead.

clusters.headline: Malawi: Inside Malawi's Public Sector Shake-Up - Minister Demands Results As Agencies Sign Reform Deals
clusters.summary: [Nyasa Times] Malawi's Minister of Justice and Constitutional Affairs has put his foot down, demanding that heads of the country's key legal and governance bodies sign up to sweeping public sector reforms -- or explain why not.

clusters.headline: Singapore expert panel recommends targeting harmful social media features instead of imposing age bans
clusters.summary: The government-appointed panel also called for a precautionary approach to regulating social media, stronger age checks, and greater support for parents and young users.

clusters.headline: Ghana: How Do Teens Living With Disabilities in Ghana View Their Future? We Asked Them to Show Us
clusters.summary: [The Conversation Africa] About 8% of Ghana's population is disabled. A high percentage are adolescents, which could be linked to the country's dominant population of young people (15 to 35 years).

clusters.headline: Nigeria: Investigation - Gas Flares, Poisoned Lives, Regulatory Failures in Nigeria's Oil Fields
clusters.summary: [Premium Times] From disappearing fish in Akwa Ibom to polluted rainwater in Bayelsa, communities living beside Nigeria's oil facilities are confronting the human consequences of methane, a potent but largely invisible greenhouse gas.

clusters.headline: Zimbabwe: Police Ramp Up Security Ahead of Planned July 31 Shutdown Over Constitutional Changes
clusters.summary: [New Zimbabwe] THE Zimbabwe Republic Police (ZRP) says it has deployed officers across the country to maintain law and order ahead of a planned nationwide shutdown on Friday, as political tensions mount following the enactment of Constitutional Amendment Act No. 3 (CAA3).

clusters.headline: Anthony Fauci refuses to answer questions during tense US Senate hearing about Covid origins
clusters.summary: The former top US health official said he feared Republicans could try to trip him up and use his testimony to prosecute him for perjury.

clusters.headline: No more Marmite in Singapore? What this means for your favourite dishes at local restaurants
clusters.summary: Some restaurants are relying on existing stock, while others are searching for alternative ingredients and suppliers or preparing to remove Marmite dishes from their menus altogether.

clusters.headline: Are some soldiers colluding with Nigeria's criminal gangs? A recent arrest prompts questions
clusters.summary: A private's detention reignites concerns that troops are contributing to the country's security challenges.

clusters.headline: Africa: 'Am I Safe Here?' - The Question Standing Between Transgender Africans and HIV Care
clusters.summary: [allAfrica] Rio de Janeiro, Brazil -- The greatest barrier to ending AIDS among transgender people in Africa is not a lack of medicine, but laws, stigma and exclusion.
